what_its_for: Insulin detemir is a long-acting insulin used to help control blood sugar levels in adults and children with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. It works slowly over many hours to keep your blood sugar steady throughout the day and night. It is not used to treat sudden high blood sugar emergencies.
how_to_take: Inject insulin detemir under the skin (subcutaneous injection) in your stomach area, upper thigh, or upper arm. Never inject it into a vein or muscle. Rotate your injection sites each time to avoid skin lumps or thickening. Do not mix insulin detemir with any other type of insulin in the same syringe. Use a new needle for every injection. Follow your doctor or diabetes educator's instructions on exactly how to inject. If you use a pen device, prime it before each use according to the instructions that come with the pen.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe a dose that is right for you based on your blood sugar levels, diet, activity level, and other factors. You may take it once a day at the same time each day, or twice a day (morning and evening). The dose is different for every person. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first. Always use the dose your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, check your blood sugar right away. If your blood sugar is high, contact your doctor for guidance on what to do. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. To help remember, try taking your dose at the same time every day. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store unopened (unused) insulin detemir vials or pens in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it — throw it away if it has been frozen. Once you open (start using) a vial or pen, you can keep it at room temperature (below 86°F / 30°C) for up to 42 days. Keep it away from direct heat, sunlight, and extreme cold. Always check the expiration date before using. Discard used needles and syringes safely in a sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can cause your blood sugar to drop too low (hypoglycemia). Do not skip meals after taking your insulin dose. Avoid strenuous or unusual exercise without checking with your doctor first, as it can lower your blood sugar. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, shaky, or your blood sugar is low. Avoid changing your diet, activity level, or insulin brand without telling your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) such as shakiness, sweating, dizziness, confusion, fast heartbeat, or fainting. Also call if you have signs of high blood sugar (hyperglycemia) such as increased thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision, or fruity breath. Call your doctor if you notice skin changes at your injection site (lumps, pits, or redness), if you gain weight unexpectedly, or if you are sick, stressed, or have surgery planned, as these can change your insulin needs. Seek emergency help immediately if you lose consciousness.
when_it_works: Insulin detemir starts working about 1 to 2 hours after you inject it. It has a slow, steady effect that lasts up to 24 hours. Unlike fast-acting insulin, it does not have a strong peak, which means it works more evenly throughout the day. It may take a few days to several weeks to find the right dose and see your blood sugar fully under control.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using insulin detemir if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Blood sugar control is very important during pregnancy and your insulin needs may change. Children: Insulin detemir can be used in children 2 years of age and older with type 1 diabetes. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to insulin and have a higher risk of low blood sugar. Kidney or liver problems: Your insulin dose may need to be adjusted if you have kidney or liver disease. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and medications.
